name: CI Fast Feedback
description: Structure CI pipelines to run fastest checks first and fail early to minimize developer wait time.
content:
# CI Fast Feedback Rules

- Order checks from fastest to slowest — lint (seconds) before unit tests (minutes) before E2E tests (minutes+)
- Fail fast — if linting fails, don't waste time running the full test suite
- Use parallelism — split test suites across multiple runners to reduce wall-clock time
- Cache dependencies aggressively — `node_modules`, Python virtualenvs, Go modules, Docker layers
- Use incremental builds — only rebuild and retest what changed when possible
- Keep the total CI time under 10 minutes for the critical path — developers context-switch when CI takes longer
- Run expensive checks (E2E, security scans, performance tests) only on PRs to main, not every push
- Use matrix builds for cross-platform testing — run OS and version combinations in parallel
- Set timeouts on CI jobs — prevent hung processes from blocking the pipeline indefinitely
- Report test results with JUnit XML or similar — show failures inline in the PR, not buried in logs
- Use CI status checks as merge gates — don't allow merging with failing required checks
- Monitor CI pipeline duration over time — alert when builds consistently exceed your target time
